Subject: High p99 latency spikes on inference endpoint - urgent

Hi Mateo,

We started seeing dramatic p99 spikes on our /v1/generate endpoint around 15:50 UTC on May 15th. p95 is mostly fine (~220ms) but p99 jumps to 6-8s in short bursts and a subset of requests stall for >12s. This started after a traffic surge from a batch job — steady qps of ~140 ramped to 430 for ~10 minutes.

Attached is a trace sample (nb_latency_trace_20270515.json) and a short profile from our side. The errors are not timeouts — responses eventually come back but with long tails, which is causing falling-through retries and user-facing failures.

Can you triage? We need an exec-level update in the next 2 hours; our CS and SRE teams are on a call.

Thanks,
Priya

On Sat, May 15, 2027 at 16:28, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads up, Priya — we got the trace. Monica/Marcus/Lauren, looping you in for immediate triage.

I pulled the traces and correlating logs. Short summary:
- Root cause (likely): rapid QPS ramp caused a wave of requests that missed the prefix/KV cache on multiple hosts. That produces an expensive recompute path plus increased KV cache write amplification.
- Mechanism: per-tenant concurrency cap is enforced at the front proxy. When upstream workers slow (cache recompute), the proxy queues requests — this cascades into request buffering and head-of-line blocking on a small subset of worker shards. That shows up as elevated p99 (~6–12s) while p50/p95 remain ok.
- Evidence: consistent worker shards X/Y showing async IO spikes and long kernel exec times; high retry counts from client-side.

Short-term mitigations (can do within minutes):
1) Lift the tenant concurrency cap for NorthBridge from 250 -> 500 for the next 30 minutes (temporary override).
2) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching policy (cache warmup) for their tenants — reduces recompute.
3) Force-route a fraction (~30%) of traffic to a lower-memory quantized model variant to shed heavy token cost.
4) If still degrading, apply request-level shed (reject with 429 for non-critical burst traffic) to avoid retry storms.

I can push 1+2 immediately (5–10m) from infra console; 3 requires coordination with routing service (another 5–15m).

Runbook reference: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-playbook-link (Request funneling & backpressure runbook).

I’ll start with 1 & 2 and monitor; updating JIRA-INC-4821.

— Marcus

Aditya/Markus — quick exec summary and ask:

What happened: a short traffic surge resulted in request funneling on-front proxy + KV-cache miss wave on a subset of worker shards, producing p99 spikes (6–12s) while p95 remained acceptable. Evidence and mitigations are in JIRA-INC-4821 and attached trace.

What we did (hours):
- Marcus temporarily raised tenant concurrency cap and enabled aggressive prefix caching at 17:10 UTC.
- Routed 30% of traffic to quantized variant for 20 minutes to shed heavy executions.
- Monitoring: p99 reduced from 8s -> ~420ms over 22 minutes; no customer-visible errors after mitigations, customer retries decreased.

Customer impact: brief SLA risk window (approx 18 minutes), headers show elevated retry counts; NorthBridge requested exec credit consideration and a short postmortem.

Ask: can we approve a one-time goodwill credit (equivalent to 10% of April usage billed to NorthBridge) to cover customer churn risk? If approvals are needed I can surface a draft reconciliation.

Next steps: full postmortem scheduled 48 hours after event; Marcus to prepare root-cause writeup and regression tests for cache warmup. Monica to coordinate customer communications.

— Mateo

Update after monitoring: temporary changes are complete and we’ve reverted the concurrency override at 10:55 UTC after confirming stable p99 behavior. Root-cause hypothesis and follow-ups:

- Primary trigger: request funneling + cold prefix-cache misses when a burst originates from a client-side batch. The cache miss storm amplified I/O on a few worker shards and exposed a serialization point in the recompute path.
- Engineering actions: add cache warmup heuristics for bursty tenants; add autoscale guard to detect KV miss waves and proactively spin additional worker shards; add a throttling rule to the proxy that prefers 429 early rather than buffering indefinitely.
- Customer comms: Monica to send a short executive postmortem and schedule a joint run-through of the playbook.

I’ll upload the detailed trace + flame graphs to the drive link and post the RCA to JIRA-INC-4821.

— Marcus
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
